messages:
Eve (Finance): FYI vendor 'DataStream AS' (Norway) sent a March invoice with NOK amounts and flagged that they need a W-9 for US withholding. They also included an EU-style VAT number (looks like NO12345678).

Ravi (Accounting): Norway VAT is called MVA. If they're charging MVA and Redwood has no Norwegian registration, likely incorrect for exported services. Also W-9 request is wrong for foreign vendor. We should ask for W-8BEN-E.

Nora (Vendor): Hi Redwood team, I've attached invoice. We're a Norwegian entity but sell to global customers. Our tax advisor suggested adding gross-up language when dealing with US customers. We can provide W-8BEN-E if required.

Eve (Finance): Please send W-8BEN-E signed and a corrected invoice without gross-up and without MVA if applicable. If your advisor insists otherwise, please include their memo.

TaxBot: Quick action items:
- Request W-8BEN-E and company MVA certificate.
- Ask vendor to reissue invoice in USD or GBP for easier payment conversion.
- Do not accept W-9 from non-US entities.
- If vendor continues to ask for gross-up, escalate to Legal.

Ravi (Accounting): Also note to AP team: if we get a W-8BEN-E and it shows foreign status, set withholding to zero in Netsuite unless treaty states otherwise. Save docs under vendor profile.

Nora (Vendor): Sending the W-8BEN-E and MVA cert now. Also sending the tax advisor memo.

Eve (Finance): Received 1: will review and confirm. If MVA was charged in error, ask them to credit VAT or issue corrected invoice.

TaxBot: FYI: Norway has reverse-charge rules for B2B digital services; vendor should not charge MVA for non-Norwegian business customers.

Eve (Finance): Thanks. Closing once we've confirmed corrected invoice and W-8 is saved.
